summary: Super Smash entries from Sami's spine and sourced supplemental seeds, built for per-platform route research.

entries.title: Super Smash Bros.

emulation.notes: Use the Nintendo 64 release with an accurate N64 emulator such as ares or simple64; use clean upscaling and original timing.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: High for N64: modern accurate emulation can improve output while preserving the original release.

primary.why: The original entry is sourced for Nintendo 64, with a later iQue Player release. Nintendo 64 is the main archive route for the original version; iQue is a regional later release and not a higher-fidelity complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Nintendo 64 release with an accurate N64 emulator such as ares or simple64; use clean upscaling and original timing.

entries.remaster_caveats: The iQue Player release is tracked as a later regional release, not a remaster or replacement primary.

entries.definitive_edition: Super Smash Bros. Brawl on Wii

emulation.notes: Use the Wii release in Dolphin with internal-resolution scaling; keep original controls and content behavior.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: High: Dolphin can upscale the Wii release cleanly.

primary.version: Super Smash Bros. Brawl on Wii
primary.why: Wii is the release platform for this entry, so the original Wii version is the complete archive route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Wii release in Dolphin with internal-resolution scaling; keep original controls and content behavior.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster split; use the final official update/DLC set where applicable.

entries.title: Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS

emulation.notes: Use original 3DS hardware or a compatible 3DS emulator with the final game update and owned DLC where applicable.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Good: fidelity is limited by dual-screen 3DS design, though clean capture/emulation can improve readability.

primary.why: This local row is specifically the Nintendo 3DS version. Platform-specific 3DS features include Smash Run and StreetSmash, so the 3DS build itself is the primary for this entry.
primary.how_to_play: Use original 3DS hardware or a compatible 3DS emulator with the final game update and owned DLC where applicable.

entries.remaster_caveats: Official Nintendo 3DS/Wii U online services ended in 2024; preserve local/offline modes and final update/DLC content where owned.

entries.title: Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and Wii U
entries.definitive_edition: Wii U version with 3DS secondary for exclusives

emulation.notes: Use Wii U/Cemu for the main HD route; use 3DS hardware/emulation for Smash Run and 3DS-specific content.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Wii U emulation for primary; 3DS emulation for secondary

primary.why: The Wii U version has HD output, 8-Player Smash, and the strongest fidelity route, while the 3DS version has exclusive modes and handheld-themed stages.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Wii U version on Wii U hardware or Cemu with all desired DLC; play the 3DS version separately for Smash Run and its exclusive handheld content.

secondary.exclusive_content: Smash Run, StreetSmash, stereoscopic 3D presentation, and 3DS-exclusive stages/trophies.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the 3DS version's exclusive modes and stages after the Wii U main route.
secondary.why: The 3DS and Wii U versions have platform-specific modes, stages, trophies, and features rather than being identical ports.

entries.remaster_caveats: Official Nintendo 3DS and Wii U online services ended, affecting online play.

entries.title: Super Smash Bros. Ultimate
entries.definitive_edition: Ultimate with Fighters Pass Vol. 1 and Vol. 2 DLC

primary.version: Ultimate with Fighters Pass Vol. 1 and Vol. 2 DLC
primary.why: Ultimate includes every previous fighter in its base roster and adds more fighters, stages, and music through DLC; the Switch release with all DLC is the most complete official Smash route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Super Smash Bros. Ultimate on Nintendo Switch or Switch 2 backward compatibility with Fighters Pass Vol. 1, Fighters Pass Vol. 2, and remaining individual DLC installed.

entries.remaster_caveats: DLC ownership determines full roster/stage/music completeness.
